chunks: And it is narrated from ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, who said:

I asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man who rents from another man a house or a ship for a year, more than that, or less. He said: “The lease is binding until the time for which it was rented, and the choice regarding taking the rent belongs to its owner: if he wishes, he takes it, and if he wishes, he leaves it.”

key_terms.السَّفِينَةَ: the ship or boat being leased
key_terms.الْوَقْتِ: the specified term or agreed period

ai.seo_question: Is a lease binding until the end of its agreed term in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on leasing property such as a house or a ship for a specified period. It states that the lease remains binding until the agreed term ends, while the owner has discretion regarding whether to take the rent or forgo it.
